boundary_rationale: A third-person topic shift opens the row: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.” web:Job.6.14 (Hebrew לַמָּ֣ס מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ חָ֑סֶד וְיִרְאַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲזֽוֹב, oshb:Job.6.14, grammatically third-person throughout -- the friend-word carries a 3ms suffix and the verb is 3ms imperfect, with no vocative particle), pivoting the subject-matter from Job's own exhaustion to a gnomic charge against companions in general. He extends the charge with the brook-caravan metaphor, “My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;” web:Job.6.15, traces the image through the melting ice and vanishing caravans of web:Job.6.16-Job.6.20, then the address itself turns second-person for the first time in the unit, “For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.” web:Job.6.21 (Hebrew כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה הֱיִ֣יתֶם לא ל֑וֹ תִּֽרְא֥וּ חֲ֝תַ֗ת וַתִּירָֽאוּ, oshb:Job.6.21 -- the quoted span crosses the verse's ketiv/qere adjacency at לא ל֑וֹ, WLC single-witness, ketiv and qere standing adjacent in the extract; the verse's three finite verbs, הֱיִ֣יתֶם, תִּֽרְא֥וּ and וַתִּירָֽאוּ, are all second-person plural), before closing on a pair of denials that he ever asked the friends for a gift or ransom, web:Job.6.22-Job.6.23. This second-person address shift at 6:21 is a genuine tier-1 signal, not mere texture; it runs unbroken to the end of the chapter, and it is disclosed here as a live internal candidate for this unit's own seam rather than dismissed. It is not adopted as the row's own edge because the third-person charge and its direct application are held together as one movement of the friend-rebuke closing on Job's self-examination through 6:23; the alternative seam at 6:20|6:21 is disclosed here as a live, comparably warranted rival rather than resolved.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking the row at Job.6.20|Job.6.21 for the second-person turn there is a live rival, not a texture-only consideration: 6:21 opens the unit's first 2mp forms and second-person address runs unbroken through 6:29 (nine verses, Job.6.21-Job.6.29), a comparably or better-warranted internal seam than the 6:23|6:24 edge kept here. It is disclosed rather than adopted because the row is held as one continuous rebuke of the friends across the third-person charge and its direct application; the question is left open rather than resolved, in the same spirit as the frame's own disclosed 2:6|2:7 crux.
literature_type_guess: friends rebuke: why abandon one brought low and helpless

boundary_rationale: A topic-turn interrogative opens the row's final movement: מָֽה אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ (oshb:Job.7.17), “What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,” web:Job.7.17, continuing the direct address to God with the daily scrutiny of web:Job.7.18, the plea “How long will you not look away from me” web:Job.7.19, and the accusation of being made a “mark” and a “burden” web:Job.7.20 -- a verse that itself carries a paseq segment, tier-3 and single-witness -- closing the speech on “Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I will not be.” web:Job.7.21. That closing verse also carries a petuchah notation and a paseq segment, both single-witness and both tier-3 at most, corroborating rather than driving the close of the reply here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Job.7.17-Job.7.21 into the preceding row was rejected: the verse-initial topic-turn interrogative opening oshb:Job.7.17, מָֽה אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ, pivots from Job's own life-loathing at Job.7.16 to the what-is-man question put to God, marking this row's own opening seam rather than a mere continuation of the Job.7.11 resolve's aftermath; the merge this rejects is INSIDE this book's ~4-12 vv strophe guide (Job.7.11-Job.7.21 = 11 verses), so length itself carries no rejection weight here.
literature_type_guess: closing plea: divine scrutiny of man and the unanswered request for pardon

boundary_rationale: An explicit quotative frame opens this short strophe: אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל כֵּ֥ן (glossed ‘it is all one; therefore I say’, Job.9.22), introducing the indictment “he destroys the blameless and the wicked” web:Job.9.22. This opening word, תָּ֥ם (‘blameless’), repeats — at SKELETON tier (the pointed forms differ: merkha at Job.9.22, meteg at Job.9.20 and Job.9.21, which are byte-identical to each other) — the word that twice closes the preceding strophe's argument (תָּֽם at Job.9.20 word 5, תָּֽם at Job.9.21 word 1), a cross-seam lexical bond disclosed here rather than left implicit; it corroborates continuity of the courtroom-to-indictment argument across 9.21|9.22 without moving either strophe's edge. Job.9.23-Job.9.24 extend the same indictment: Job.9.22's מְכַלֶּֽה (‘destroys’) carries an explicit third-person subject, ה֣וּא, and Job.9.23's verse-final יִלְעָֽג (‘mocks’) has no expressed subject of its own — WEB's own rendering keeps the pronoun 'he' across the verse boundary rather than naming 'the scourge' as a fresh subject, so the mocking agent is left as open a question in the Hebrew as in English; either way the indictment stays continuous, reaching “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked” web:Job.9.24, closing on the rhetorical question “If not he, then who is it?” web:Job.9.24. The subject shifts from this cosmic indictment to Job's own fleeting days at Job.9.25, marking the strophe's far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding Job.9.22-Job.9.24 into the preceding courtroom-inability argument was rejected given the explicit inferential frame that opens Job.9.22 and the fresh third-person subject (earth, judges) it introduces.
literature_type_guess: theodicy indictment: God mocks the calamity of innocent

boundary_rationale: Job turns from describing the assault to his own response to it, fronting the object of his mourning ritual: שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י, “I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.” (web:Job.16.15), continued in his physical distress, “My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids,” (web:Job.16.16), and closing on a protest of innocence, “although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.” (web:Job.16.17). The unit opening at Job.16.9 also fronts a term before its verb (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף, oshb:Job.16.9), as does Job.16.12 inside it (שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי, 'I was at ease'), so word order alone does not distinguish this row's edge; what changes at Job.16.15 is Job's grammatical role, from the described object of a third-person assault (Job.16.9-Job.16.14) to the grammatical subject of his own 1cs acts (שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי, 'I have sewed') — a participant-role shift, not the fronting by itself, marks the topic turn to Job's own mourning and innocence, a short unit that ends before the vocative apostrophe to the earth opens the next row.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 16:15-17 as a continuation of the assault sequence would miss the fronted object that marks Job's own response as a new topic.
literature_type_guess: Weeping into dust with face-transformation imagery

boundary_rationale: The speaker-change seam at Job.21.34|Job.22.1 opens this row: Job's speech, opened by וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.21.1, ends at Job.21.34 (וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל וּ֝תְשֽׁוּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם נִשְׁאַר מָֽעַל, a 2mp address to the friends, followed by SAMEKH), and this row opens with Eliphaz answering instead (וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.22.1; “Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,” web:Job.22.1). The formula's epithet is spelled defectively here (הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י) against the fuller spelling Eliphaz's first two formula instances carry (הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י, oshb:Job.4.1 and oshb:Job.15.1); swept independently, the defective spelling occurs at Job.22.1 alone (sweep: 1 book-wide) while the fuller spelling occurs 5 times book-wide, both in formula position and in narration (oshb:Job.2.11, oshb:Job.4.1, oshb:Job.15.1, oshb:Job.42.7, oshb:Job.42.9). Four verse-initial ha-interrogative tokens open this row in sequence — הַלְאֵ֥ל (Job.22.2), הַחֵ֣פֶץ (Job.22.3), הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ (Job.22.4), הֲלֹ֣א (Job.22.5) — the first three of which WEB's own punctuation further unpacks into four question-marked clauses, since Job.22.3's second colon (וְאִם בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ) is also rendered as a question though it opens on a mid-verse וְאִם rather than a fresh he-token; Job.22.5's הֲלֹ֣א (oshb:Job.22.5) sharpens the charge from piety to outright wickedness, setting up the itemized list that follows without yet stating it. Eliphaz's fifth ha-interrogative in this speech falls outside this row, at Job.22.12, and a sixth and final one opens Job.22.15 (הַאֹ֣רַח, oshb:Job.22.15).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at Job.22.4 and treating Job.22.5 as an opening line of the accusation catalogue was rejected, since Job.22.5 is still framed as an interrogative continuing the ha-prefixed question series of Job.22.2-Job.22.4, against the declarative register the catalogue itself uses from Job.22.6 on — a register contrast, not an asyndetic one: three of the catalogue's six verses (Job.22.6, Job.22.8, Job.22.11) open on overt connectives (כִּֽי, וְאִ֣ישׁ, אוֹ) rather than asyndetically, Job.22.6 itself a subordinating ki-clause.
literature_type_guess: Eliphaz's third-cycle response opening with piety-premise

boundary_rationale: Address shifts from third-person description of the wicked to direct second-person imperative at the row's near edge: after the quoted maxim of the wicked's fate, אִם לֹ֣א נִכְחַ֣ד קִימָ֑נוּ (oshb:Job.22.20, third-person plural), the row opens on הַסְכֶּן נָ֣א עִמּ֑וֹ (oshb:Job.22.21, “Acquaint yourself with him now, and be at peace” web:Job.22.21), a direct second-person imperative -- an address shift at Job.22.20|Job.22.21. Eliphaz's closing appeal runs unbroken from that imperative through the return-to-Shaddai protasis (אִם תָּשׁ֣וּב עַד שַׁ֭דַּי תִּבָּנֶ֑ה, oshb:Job.22.23), the further imperative of oshb:Job.22.24 (וְשִׁית עַל עָפָ֥ר בָּ֑צֶר), and the waw-qatal consequent of oshb:Job.22.25 (וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ, “The Almighty will be your treasure” web:Job.22.25); the appeal's own imperative-to-promise register shift therefore falls inside this span, at Job.22.24|Job.22.25, and is disclosed here as internal texture rather than a further seam. כִּי אָ֭ז (oshb:Job.22.26, “For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty” web:Job.22.26) continues, rather than reopens, that same result movement -- no renewed protasis, address-shift or formula marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 -- and the appeal carries through the answered-prayer and decreed-authority material of Job.22.27-Job.22.29 to its close at Job.22.30 (יְֽמַלֵּ֥ט אִֽי נָקִ֑י וְ֝נִמְלַ֗ט בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפֶּֽיךָ), where the row's own second-person address to the friend ends. A petuchah follows Job.22.30 (oshb:Job.22.30 (petuchah, single-witness)), corroborating -- at Writings tier-3 weak strength, not as a driver -- the row's far edge, where Job's own speech formula opens the next row (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.23.1).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the appeal at Job.22.24|Job.22.25, where the imperative gives way to sustained promise, is a live but weaker rival: וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Job.22.25) is the consequence of the conditions set in Job.22.23-Job.22.24, and cutting a conditional sentence between its condition and its consequence is not a protasis/apodosis-block edge under this book's seam law (a block begins at a fresh protasis, as in the chapter-31 im-series); the register shift is disclosed here as texture inside the row rather than adopted as a further edge.
literature_type_guess: Eliphaz's closing appeal: return to Shaddai as treasure, with the promised delight, answered prayer, and rescue for the humble that follow

boundary_rationale: אִם שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י ..., “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’” (web:Job.31.24), opens a materialism sequence containing three independently verse-initial protases, not two: trust in gold (Job.31.24), a further wealth-increase clause (Job.31.25, אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י..., “If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great” web:Job.31.25), and astral reverence for sun and moon (Job.31.26, אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל ...וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ, “if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,” web:Job.31.26). One apodosis follows at Job.31.28 (גַּם ה֭וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י, “this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for I would have denied the God who is above” web:Job.31.28), the verdict-formula עון פלילי that elsewhere at Job.31.11 closes one oath immediately preceding it (protasis Job.31.9, apodosis Job.31.10) rather than binding several protases together; the additive גַּם that opens Job.31.28 most directly continues from the astral material immediately before it (Job.31.26-Job.31.27) rather than reaching back to bind the wealth protases of Job.31.24-Job.31.25 into the same apodosis. That reading is disclosed as a live rival, not adopted: the row is chunked as written, with all three protases and the one following apodosis held inside its own span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A plausible alternative treats wealth (Job.31.24-Job.31.25) and celestial worship (Job.31.26-Job.31.28) as two separate oaths, each with its own protasis clauses; the verdict-formula parallel with Job.31.11 (skeleton sweep of עון פלילי: 2 book-wide, Job.31.11 and Job.31.28) is disclosed as corroboration for reading Job.31.28's apodosis as answering the immediately preceding astral protasis specifically, rather than as one warrant spanning all three protases of this row, without redrawing the row's own frozen edges.
literature_type_guess: Oath against trust in gold and reverence for sun and moon, closing on the verdict of denying God above
